summary.title: The Art of Multiprocessor Programming (2nd Edition)
summary.one_liner: A textbook covering how to program multiple threads sharing memory, from simple spin locks to concurrent data structures and transactional memory.
keywords: how to write thread-safe data structures
takeaways: Understand how multiple threads access shared memory and the basics of synchronization.
Learn the design of concurrent data structures such as lists, queues, stacks, hash tables and skiplists.
Study synchronization primitives from simple locks through to transactional memory systems.
Learn the relative power of synchronization operations and the universality of consensus.
summary.summary: The Art of Multiprocessor Programming, Second Edition (September 2020) by Herlihy, Shavit, Luchangco and Spear is a textbook on multicore programming. The page lists its 20 chapters, which move from mutual exclusion and concurrent objects through the consensus hierarchy to concurrent lists, queues, stacks, hashing, skiplists, priority queues, scheduling, barriers and transactional programming. The second edition adds new exercises and examples for instructors. The book targets students in multiprocessor courses and working engineers, and the listing describes it as a self-contained text with many examples.
